Fredrik Esscher had already introduced exponential tilting in 1932 to approximate the tail of an insurance claims distribution, and the blocker for exact tilting today, the value function at strong tilts, is a tail estimate of the same kind.

The applied mathematicians Tabak and Vanden-Eijnden gave an early formulation of normalizing flows in 2010, and Neural ODEs made flows continuous in 2018, trained with an adjoint method credited to Pontryagin. FFJORD trained them by maximum likelihood at the cost of an ODE solve per training step, and Noé's Boltzmann generators used flows in 2019 to sample molecular equilibrium states. Diffusion models began in 2015 with an idea Sohl-Dickstein and coauthors called "inspired by non-equilibrium statistical physics," built on the Jarzynski equality and annealed importance sampling. By 2020 the ingredients existed, short of a way to train a continuous flow without integrating it.

The 2022 bet and the diffusion objection

Three groups bet within a month in 2022 that the noising process and its reversal were scaffolding. Liu, Gong, and Liu called straight paths "the shortest paths between two points." Albergo and Vanden-Eijnden wrote that "we can bypass this diffusion completely." Lipman, Chen, and three coauthors said flow matching "subsumes existing diffusion paths as specific instances" and borrowed McCann's 1997 term, displacement interpolation, which describes each pinned path exactly and the averaged flow only loosely. Chen had co-written FFJORD, whose training method the new paper retired.

Diffusion researchers answered that the novelty was a reparameterization. Kingma and Gao showed in March 2023 that "all commonly used diffusion model objectives equate to a weighted integral of ELBOs over different noise levels," which made flow matching one more weighting, and in December 2024 Gao and five Google DeepMind colleagues wrote that "diffusion models and Gaussian flow matching are the same."

Industrial studies sided with the objection on substance. Stability's March 2024 study of 61 formulations for SD3 found that "only rectified flow formulations with modified timestep sampling perform better than" its diffusion baseline, and Movie Gen's October 2024 paper found flow matching "more robust to the exact choice of noise schedules" than the diffusion loss it beat in an ablation. The transport camp won the framing anyway, because its regression extended with less machinery to chosen couplings, data at both ends, manifolds, discrete states, and, through Generator Matching, any Markov process.

Rectified flow's narrower bet, that straight paths would allow one-step sampling because a straight path integrates exactly in one Euler step, lost. Rectified Diffusion answered in 2024 that "straightness is not an essential training target," Hertrich, Chambolle, and Delon built counterexamples in 2025 where rectified flows miss optimal transport maps, and few-step products went to adversarial distillation.

How the branches formed

Regressing the integral gave the one-step line. After OpenAI's consistency models in 2023, Boffi, Albergo, and Vanden-Eijnden made the two-time flow map the target in 2024, and Kaiming He's group set one-step ImageNet records with MeanFlow in 2025. The same group's Drifting took the record in 2026 with no ODE, matching distributions in pretrained features, and a successor trained on the features FID itself uses scored 0.72, which ended the benchmark. Flow maps keep one thing no rival has, a cheap lookahead from any noise level to the endpoint, which reward search in protein co-folding already uses.

Regressing jump rates of continuous-time Markov chains gave the discrete branch, and SEDD won an ICML 2024 best paper after plain masked cross-entropy had already matched it. Masked diffusion is equivalent to order-agnostic autoregression, a scheme Uria, Murray, and Larochelle introduced in 2013, and Edit Flows descend from the 2019 Levenshtein Transformer. Consecutive ICML award committees backed opposite claims about decoding order, adaptive order in 2025 and left-to-right order for reasoning in 2026. The largest released models that state an origin, DiffusionGemma among them, are converted autoregressive checkpoints that decode left to right in blocks.

Data at both ends revived Schrödinger. De Bortoli, Thornton, Heng, and Doucet built their 2021 solver to spare generation a long noising run to a Gaussian and presented it as a continuous version of the Sinkhorn algorithm, and DSBM replaced its iterations in 2023 with bridge matching, which recovers flow matching as a limit. The bridges that work at scale, in particle-physics unfolding and NVIDIA's speech toolkit, train on paired data, which hands them the coupling and brings them close to conditional flow matching under an older name. Unpaired bridges survive in single-cell biology, where minimum-action reconstructions return curl-free dynamics by construction, which snapshots cannot test.

A reward at one end gave the tilting branch. Kevin Black, later an author of π0, ran policy gradients through the denoising chain in DDPO in 2023, the inference camp built sequential Monte Carlo samplers such as twisted SMC, and Adjoint Matching showed in 2024 that naive KL-regularized fine-tuning misses the tilt unless it runs under a memoryless noise schedule. Image fine-tuning and molecular sampling share the target p_base·exp(r/β) and rarely share evaluations, because they trust their rewards differently. An energy is the truth up to the potential's error, so sampler papers chase exactness and get judged against parallel tempering. An image reward is a proxy that gets hacked, so production recipes leave the tilt on purpose through DPO, GRPO without a KL term, or noise levels chosen for accuracy and stability. Outside one 16-robot QAM deployment, nothing that ships samples the exact tilt, including classifier-free guidance, which provably samples a different distribution.

In control the tilted target is π_β·exp(τQ), the behavior policy tilted by its critic. Diffusion Policy made generative models a robot policy class in 2023, and π0 put a flow-matching action expert on a vision-language model in 2024. Levine's Berkeley group then fit flow policies to that target with Q-learning with adjoint matching in 2026. Physical Intelligence, in a paper Levine coauthored, instead shipped a recipe that conditions the flow on a binarized advantage, and its π0.7 distills RL specialists' rollouts through quality labels. On August 7, 2026, the Simons Institute scheduled Levine on how expressive policies "changed how we use continuous actions," then Max Simchowitz, coauthor of a study finding that a two-step regression policy matches flow policies, on "Do we need diffusion in robotics?"

Collisions

Flow matching retired the adjoint from training generators, and Adjoint Matching brought it back for fine-tuning in 2024, citing Kappen's path integrals. Meta then built a molecular sampler on it, Qiyang Li and Levine built QAM, and Domingo-Enrich and Han rederived it from the stochastic maximum principle. GRPO crossed the other way, from DeepSeek-R1 to image models within four months in Flow-GRPO and DanceGRPO, which turned the flow's ODE back into an SDE and so reinstated the noise rectified flow had removed.

Where money entered

Meta, the lab that published flow matching, was first to scale it, and in 2025 it agreed to pay Black Forest Labs about $140M, a company three SD3 authors had launched on flow matching in August 2024, and licensed Midjourney's technology, which suggests that owning the method did not give Meta the product. Most one-step work came from companies that pay to sample at scale, among them OpenAI, Stability, NVIDIA, ByteDance, and Luma, which reads as inference bills buying the agenda, though none has said so.

The papers' own authors commercialized diffusion language models, and Inception, which Stefano Ermon leads, closed a $50M round in November 2025. Image, video, and serving companies raised far more, at least $3.4B from January 2025 to October 2026, a floor this run summed from eight companies' announced rounds: Black Forest Labs $300M, Runway $308M and $315M, Luma $900M, Stability $76M, ShengShu about $381M, fal $125M and $140M, Decart $100M and $300M, and Higgsfield $80M and $400M. The sum leaves out most of the nearly RMB 30B that four Chinese video companies reported in mid-2026. Biohub's virtual biology initiative, about $1.8B of cash and in-kind backing by October 2026, buys measurement, which this record suggests is the binding constraint.

The graveyard

Maximum-likelihood flow training, iterative bridge fitting, and SEDD's score entropy each lost to a simpler objective. Continuous embedding diffusion for language died of a likelihood gap after 2023. Sander Dieleman wrote in January 2023 that "it is still too early to consider diffusion as a serious alternative to autoregression" while favoring the continuous route. In August 2026 he wrote that "continuous diffusion for language went extinct," then gave the reason for its return: "This distillability advantage is probably the main reason why CDLMs are back with a vengeance today." A line that lost on likelihood came back once distillation became the constraint, the clearest rediscovery in this record.

Built-in rotation equivariance gave way to augmentation when Proteina followed AlphaFold 3, and continuous-flow Boltzmann generators for peptides gave way to transformer flows and then an autoregressive model, all trained on simulations of related peptides. Diffusion ensembles were the leading candidate for operational weather forecasting in 2024, until ECMWF made a CRPS-trained model operational in 2025, citing accuracy as well as cost, and Google DeepMind replaced GenCast with a model trained on a proper scoring rule, a family the 2015 diffusion paper had listed among approaches to improve on.

Four losers returned in new roles: GANs as the finishing loss in few-step distillation, normalizing flows through TarFlow, whose authors found them in 2024 "more powerful than previously believed," policy gradients as GRPO, and autoregression in peptide sampling. The benchmarks died faster than the methods. One-step ImageNet FID, OpenWebText generative perplexity, GenEval, and Lennard-Jones energy distances stopped separating methods between 2024 and 2026, and the field's issue threads complain that papers set their own targets, so tables rarely compare like with like.

The live argument

Across the branches, credit went to timestep weighting at Stability, representation learning for image quality, search plus an assay in the 2026 binder campaigns, scoring rules in weather, and RL-generated data at Physical Intelligence. The confident position most likely to look foolish by 2029 is the premise of most method papers, that the next gain comes from a better transport objective.

Language is the sharpest case. Menlo Ventures wrote in March 2026 that "For the first time, a diffusion model matched the quality of autoregressive models on text generation and ran 10x faster." Four months later Google's DiffusionGemma report put its converted model 15 to 19 points behind its autoregressive parent on AIME 2026, depending on whether the parent decodes with multi-token prediction, and behind it on throughput past about 32 concurrent requests. As such, diffusion's likelier future is as a decoding mode or drafter inside autoregressive serving. One unrun experiment could reverse that, a billion-parameter diffusion model against a regularized autoregressive one on matched unique data, testing the claim that diffusion keeps learning from repeated data after autoregression saturates.

Three fights lack the evidence for a verdict. Reinforce Adjoint Matching and Tilt Matching, the regression methods for tilting posted in May 2026 and December 2025, claim speedups no outside group has rerun. RL through the flow against RL kept off it stays open, because AGIBOT's fleet run of QAM beat its reimplementation of Physical Intelligence's recipe, 0.95 to 0.85, without holding the critic fixed. Nobody has tested at scale whether flow maps matter more as lookahead than as fast samplers. The Virtual Cell Challenge's zero-shot round, a public test of transport models against statistical baselines, reports in late November 2026.

Learned sampling holds 25 of the map's 110 open problems and 2 of the roster's 42 startups. Reward tilting, the target five of the eight avenues share, holds 10 open problems and no startup, while media generation holds 6 open problems and 18 startups. Organization counts join the landscape roster to the map's sub-problems, so they are floors. Each money line condenses the avenue's header, which follows in full, and the discrete-language line adds DiffuSpace's rounds, disclosed in October, from the landscape.

Learned sampling from unnormalized densities

Training generative models to produce the states a physical system occupies at equilibrium, or the paths it takes between them, from its energy function alone or from simulations of related systems, so that chemists and physicists can skip slow simulation.

Now
No revenue yet. No company surfaced in this run sells a learned sampler, and BioEmu, Microsoft's ensemble emulator, ships under the MIT license [T1]. The nearest venture bet is Achira, a $33M seed led by Dimension in February 2025 for hybrid ML and physics simulation models [T1]. The addressed market is molecular simulation software, led by Schrödinger at $199.5M of 2025 software revenue (Business Wire, Feb 25 2026) [T1]. Research spend is larger and mostly unsized: seven lattice QCD projects in a December 2024 mailing-list post of 2025 INCITE awards held about 7.1M node-hours [T1], roughly $57M to $114M a year of cloud-equivalent compute at an assumed $8 to $16 per node-hour [T2].
In 15 years
[T3] Near zero as a standalone product through 2035, with the value captured as features inside simulation software, drug programs, and DOE allocations. If a learned sampler beats replica exchange on proteins of 50 or more residues at equal GPU-hours with a machine-learned potential, sampling becomes a core line in a market whose leader would reach about $0.5B to $0.8B of software ACV by 2036 at the 10 to 15 percent annual ACV growth it guides for 2026 and targets through 2028. That head-to-head, and whether pharma's free-energy work is limited by sampling or by force-field error, decide which.
Entry
One GPU and a few weeks for DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55, and alanine dipeptide, with open code from Meta (facebookresearch/adjoint_samplers under CC BY-NC 4.0, since the original facebookresearch/adjoint_sampling repository is archived) and the Mila group (DEM). Work that matters on peptides needs an MD corpus on the scale of ManyPeptidesMD (21,700 sequences at 200 ns each) or a machine-learned potential, plus a few GPU-weeks. Lattice work needs hep-lat collaborators and an HPC allocation.
Holy grail
A transferable model that takes an unseen protein of 50 to 100 residues with its energy function and returns reweighted equilibrium samples whose folding free energy matches long reference MD within 0.5 kcal/mol, in fewer GPU-hours than replica exchange on the same energy.
Blocker
Importance weights degrade exponentially with system size because per-particle model errors add up inside an extensive energy, so even a local model's joint effective sample size falls from 64.7 percent at 64 water molecules to 0.02 percent at 1,728, about ten effective samples in 50,000, and the methods that scale trade global reweighting for local corrections whose bias no published result bounds on heterogeneous systems such as proteins.

Language models that write by refining many token positions in parallel, through masking, uniform noise, insertions and deletions, or continuous flows, instead of emitting one token after another.

About $50M of venture into the one verified pure play, Inception's seed round led by Menlo Ventures (TechCrunch, Nov 6 2025) [T1]. No company discloses revenue. List prices are $0.20 to $0.25 per million input tokens and $0.75 per million output tokens (Inception, Feb and Oct 2026) [T1]. The large labs' models are open weights or an experimental demo.
In 15 years
[T3] Under $1B a year to standalone vendors by 2040 if diffusion becomes a decoding mode inside autoregressive serving stacks, as NVIDIA's tri-mode Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion already is. Entry
Days to weeks on one 8 to 16 GPU node. FlexMDM retrofitted LLaDA-8B in 3 days on 16 H100s, and the continuous-flow papers train 105M to 652M models on OpenWebText. Converting a 25B to 100B model takes a lab.
Holy grail
A diffusion, edit, or flow language model that matches its same-size autoregressive sibling on AIME, GPQA Diamond, and LiveCodeBench while serving more tokens per second per GPU than that sibling with multi-token prediction at 64 or more concurrent requests.
Blocker
Parallel decoding spends about 13 token positions of compute per committed token, since DiffusionGemma commits 19.7 tokens per pass over a 256-token canvas, which a one-user GPU absorbs while it waits on memory and a server batching past about 32 users pays in full, and the samplers that could commit dependent tokens in far fewer passes without factorization error exist only below 1B parameters.

Molecules, proteins, and materials

Train a model to turn noise into a protein, a drug pose, a peptide or a crystal built for one job, then find out in a lab whether it does that job.

Now
No revenue from generation itself. The money is venture plus pharma upfronts. Isomorphic Labs raised $600M (Mar 2025) and $2.1B (May 2026) and Bloomberg reported talks at $40B+ on Oct 8 2026 with nothing in the clinic, Chai Discovery raised a $400M Series C at $3.8B (company announcement, Jul 14 2026), and Generate Biomedicines listed on Nasdaq for about $400M (Feb 2026) on $31.89M of 2025 revenue against a $222.97M net loss, which is the only audited revenue figure in the avenue. All tier one.
In 15 years
Tier three. Turns on two things: whether per-target hit rates hold up on targets with no close homolog in training data, and whether anything designed this way is approved. If both, the buyer is pharma R&D and the design layer prices like a platform inside a $200B+ research budget, so tens of billions. If hit rates hold only on protein targets resembling known ones, it stays a screening accelerator sold as software and milestones, so low single-digit billions. The second outcome is the likelier one through 2035, because assay throughput sets the ceiling and is not improving at anything like the rate the generators are. A second Lilly-scale deal whose payments turn on designed-molecule performance would move this estimate up.
Entry
Weeks on one GPU to contribute to evaluation, guidance or search, because the models, weights and data are open (BoltzGen under MIT including weights and training code, Proteina and La-Proteina from NVIDIA, FrameFlow, MultiFlow, CATH and the PDB). Contributing to design itself needs a wet lab: a commercial binder assay round through Adaptyv-style services, or a collaboration with a group that already runs one. That is the gate, and it is calendar time rather than compute.
Holy grail
One conditional generator that, handed a target with no close homolog in its training data, returns twenty designs of which most work on first synthesis, across proteins, peptides, nucleic acids, small molecules and solids, with confidence calibrated well enough to skip the screen.
Blocker
Every score this avenue optimizes is a learned surrogate built from the same model family as the generator (ESMFold refolding, ipAE, Boltz-2 affinity, machine-learned interatomic potentials for stability), so in-silico numbers no longer separate methods, and the measurements that would separate them are batched, non-differentiable, weeks long, and increasingly owned by whoever runs the assay.

Flow maps and one-step generation

Training one network to jump between any two moments of a generative flow, so a sample costs one to four network calls instead of dozens, along with the rival ways of getting one-step samples that skip the flow.

Now
No company in this run's funding survey sells flow maps or any one-step method by name. The money behind the work is the inference bill of image, video, and speech generation, whose one disclosed usage-priced slice is fal at about $800M annualized revenue (The Information via Sovereign Magazine, Sep 2026), up from about $400M in Feb 2026 (Sacra) [T1-est], plus venture behind labs that publish one-step methods, such as Luma AI's $900M Series C (Nov 2025) [T1].
In 15 years
[T3] Hundreds of millions to low billions of dollars a year of avoided inference cost by 2035 to 2040 if one-step methods stay inside media, speech, and science. A cost pool in the tens of billions if a flow-map language model reaches autoregressive accuracy on reasoning in eight steps or fewer, because the method would then enter LLM serving. Language transfer decides it, video and world-model inference volume comes second, and the first branch is the likelier one.
Entry
A one-step ImageNet-256 result at B/2 scale or a 170M-parameter flow-map language model fits on one 8-GPU node for days. XL-scale image claims and anything past a few billion parameters need a JVP-capable attention kernel, public ones exist but none is a maintained general package with FSDP and context-parallel support, or a JVP-free objective, plus a multi-node budget.
Holy grail
One network trained from scratch with stock attention kernels, with no teacher and no borrowed feature encoder, that samples at any step count without quality falling as steps grow, matches the best many-step model at one or two steps on human preference and recall for 10B-parameter text-to-video, and reaches an equal-compute autoregressive model's GSM8K accuracy on text in eight steps or fewer.
Blocker
No known training signal is sharp at one step on multimodal data without either a mode-seeking adversarial or score-distillation term that costs diversity or a pretrained feature space that FID rewards, and a deterministic one-step map faces a Lipschitz lower bound that regression alone cannot get under.

Transport between datasets and scientific inference

Using generative models as priors and as maps between datasets to answer scientific questions, such as which parameters produced a gravitational wave, how a cell responds to a perturbation, or what tomorrow's weather distribution is, with uncertainty someone can check.

Now
No revenue attributable to the methods. The money is philanthropic and public research spend aimed at data. Biohub's Virtual Biology Initiative committed $500M over five years to cell data on Apr 29 2026, tier one, and grew to about $1.8B with DOE, NIH, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta on Oct 7 2026, much of it as data, compute and instruments, tier one from press coverage. Google ships WeatherNext 3 inside Search, Maps and Gemini and discloses no revenue for it.
In 15 years
Tier three. Turns on whether a large instrument collaboration such as LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA or Rubin publishes official results from an amortized flow posterior with no MCMC fallback, and whether virtual-cell models beat linear baselines zero-shot. If both, the inference layer prices as software inside pharma perturbation screening and instrument pipelines, perhaps $1B to $5B a year by 2040. If neither, it stays research spend near today's scale, a few hundred million dollars a year, about what Biohub's expanded initiative spends annually on data. The second outcome is the likelier one through 2035, because adoption here has gone to whichever method a field could check, and the checks for guided posteriors and bridges do not exist yet.
Entry
Weeks on one GPU. InverseBench, the entropic OT benchmark, the sbi and BayesFlow toolboxes, CryoBoltz and the Virtual Cell Challenge data are public. Weather at full resolution needs ERA5 and a multi-GPU node. Any claim about real data needs a partner who owns an instrument or a lineage-tracing experiment, and that costs calendar time.
Holy grail
Given a field's forward model or simulator and its real observations, a method returns posterior samples, or a coupling between two datasets, whose uncertainty is shown correct on real data, for instance nominal coverage on injected signals or predicted cell fates matching lineage barcodes, at lower cost than the method the field trusts today, which is MCMC, 4D-Var, OmniFold or Waddington-OT, with no per-problem retraining.
Blocker
Guided posteriors and flow or bridge couplings go unchecked on real data, because worst-case posterior sampling with a diffusion prior is intractable and snapshot marginals do not identify non-gradient dynamics. The one lineage-barcode scoreboard for cell couplings dates from 2020 and 2021 and has no flow or bridge entry, and the ground truth that would settle the question for cells, lineage barcodes and perturbation atlases, only began to be funded at scale in 2025 and 2026.

Reward tilting

Making a pretrained generator produce the distribution that KL-regularized reinforcement learning targets, the base model reweighted by exponentiated reward, either by fine-tuning it or by steering it while it samples, for images, molecules, robot policies, and language models alike.

Now
No revenue, product, or venture round under this name (this run's searches, Oct 2026). The nearest priced product is LLM reinforcement fine-tuning, billed at $100 per hour of training for o4-mini (OpenAI billing guide, 2025) [T1]. Post-training startups announced $83M in July and August 2026 (Deep Cogito $43M Series A, Bespoke Labs $40M, of which $31.75M was a new Series A and $8.25M an earlier raise) [T1], none selling an exact tilt. The real spend is post-training compute inside model makers, which xAI describes as RL on its 200,000-GPU cluster at pretraining scale for Grok 4 (xAI, Jul 9 2025) [T1, company claim].
In 15 years
[T3] Turns on whether trusted rewards (energies, assays, verifiers) displace learned proxies, and on whether buyers pay for calibrated samples over one best output. If both, exact tilting becomes the method layer of molecular design, scientific sampling, and verifiable-reward post-training, a slice of a post-training market plausibly worth tens of billions a year by 2040. If either fails, it stays a research toolkit with near-zero direct revenue while KL-free RL takes the money. The second is likelier through 2035 outside molecular science. An outside replication of the 2026 regression speedups at production scale would move this up.
Entry
Days on one GPU node. About 90 GPU-hours takes SD3.5-Medium from GenEval 0.24 to 0.95 with a likelihood-estimator RL recipe (Choi et al., Feb 2026), roughly $180 to $270 at an assumed $2 to $3 per GPU-hour [T2]. Tilts with closed-form answers, such as linear rewards on Gaussian mixtures, run on one GPU in hours. Power sampling on a 7B language model costs 8.84x the tokens of plain decoding (Karan and Du, Oct 2025).
Holy grail
A sampler that takes a pretrained generator and a reward it can only evaluate, returns samples from p_base·exp(r/β)/Z at any β where the tilt is computationally tractable for a small constant multiple of base cost plus a stated budget of reward calls, and passes three checks that can be run today: pass@k at or above the base model's at every k on verifiable tasks, reward histograms matching importance-weighted base samples wherever effective sample size allows, and free energies within 0.1 kcal/mol of parallel tempering at fewer energy evaluations.
Blocker
The soft value function, the base model's conditional log-mean-exp of the reward from a partial sample, has no low-variance estimator when the tilt is strong and the reward is a black box, and exactness cannot be checked outside the regimes where plain reweighting already works, so practice tunes β, the noise level, and the KL's time profile for reward against quality instead of for the tilt.

Flow and diffusion models in control

Robots and cars now generate their actions, plan, and practice inside the same flow and diffusion models that generate images, and the open question is how to improve those models from their own experience.

Now
No revenue attributable to these methods. The money is venture into robot-policy companies, more than $2.2B into robot foundation-model startups in 2025 (PitchBook data reported by The Elec, secondary) [T1-est], including Physical Intelligence's $600M Series B at $5.6B in Nov 2025 (Sacra) [T1-est], plus driving programs whose world-model spend is undisclosed, such as Wayve's $1.2B Series D at $8.6B in Feb 2026 [T1-est].
In 15 years
[T3] $3.6B to $36B a year in robot-policy licensing by 2040 if generalist manipulation reaches deployment reliability, from 1M to 10M robots at Sacra's undated $300 per robot per month. A few hundred million a year of lab R&D if it does not. Turns on whether value estimation from real experience gets solved or simulated away, and on whether world models become faithful under contact.
Entry
One GPU and the public FQL and QAM code for OGBench offline RL. One arm plus openpi for real-robot RL. Eight H100s to reproduce piRL-style RL on a flow VLA in simulation. A multi-node cluster to train a video world model.
Holy grail
A generalist robot policy that takes a new contact-rich task from about 50% to 99% success at human speed within one day of its own practice, real and simulated, with rewards and values it learns itself and no human corrections.
Blocker
Value estimation. Critics learned from hours of real-robot data are too noisy to push a flow policy far past its demonstrations, so the recipes that work on real robots use only the sign of the advantage, bound the policy to its base distribution, or lean on human corrections, and learned simulators move the same error into the world model's action faithfulness.

Entry
One node of 8 H100s for about a day reproduces Self Forcing on Wan2.1-1.3B, per its README, with the released DMD config loading Wan2.1-T2V-14B as the teacher, and distillation and streaming work runs on open checkpoints from 1.3B to 33B parameters. Training a competitive base video model is closed to newcomers.
Holy grail
A causal generator that streams 1080p video with synchronized audio at playback speed on one accelerator, keeps a scene consistent through an hour-long session, wins blind preference against the best offline model of its day, and costs under $1 per streamed hour to serve.
Blocker
Nothing supervises consistency past the teacher's clip length: causal few-step students are distilled from bidirectional teachers trained to produce clips of 5 to 30 seconds, so minute-to-hour coherence has no teacher and no reward, and its metrics are minute-scale and mutually incompatible. Position limits are no longer the wall, since LoL reported 12-hour streams with training-free RoPE jitter in January 2026 and LongLive added a KV-cache relative RoPE option for unbounded generation the same month, and neither supplies a training signal for minute 40.

What to read, in order

The spine is 4 papers, about 18 hours, in the order to read them. Each avenue's own stack follows, 53 papers in read order, and the last 39 are reference, each with a trigger for when to reach for it.

The spine4 papers, about 18 hours

  1. 1

    result

    Are we really tilting? The mechanics of reward guidance in flow and diffusion models 2026an evening

    CMU, Nicholas Boffipreprinttoo new to citedrawn in 2 figures

    Traces reward hacking in guided diffusion and flow models to plug-in estimates of the Doob h-function from finitely many particles, separates over-optimization inside a mode from failure to pick modes in closed form for Gaussian mixtures, and gives a reward-damping schedule.

    After it, guidance, fine-tuning, and best-of-N read as three ways of estimating one function, and appendix B.2, where no non-memoryless schedule recovers the tilt, is the theory under the semester project.

    skip The FLUX experiments on a first pass.
  2. 2

    survey

    Learning the integral of a diffusion model 2026two sittings

    Sander DielemanBlog post, 2026-05-06too new to citedrawn in 2 figures

    Sorts about two dozen flow-map training methods by the consistency rule they impose, compositional, Lagrangian, or Eulerian, by learning setting, and by output parameterization, and prices each in forward-pass equivalents. It is the clearest map of the flow-map design space as of May 2026.

    After it each one-step paper below lands in a cell you already know, and the semester project's results table has its columns.

    skip The catalog of MeanFlow variants on a first pass
  3. 3

    position

    No Trick, No Treat: Pursuits and Challenges Towards Simulation-free Training of Neural Samplers 2025an afternoon

    Cambridge, José Miguel Hernández-Lobato, with Jiajun He and Yuanqi DuICLR 2025 Frontiers in Probabilistic Inference workshop, per the v2 PDF's header (April 2025)no reliable countdrawn in 2 figures

    Finds that nearly all working neural samplers rely on Langevin preconditioning and that most fail to cover a simple target without it, and proposes parallel tempering plus a fitted generative model as the baseline later papers should beat.

    It is the source of the rule that a sampling claim needs a tempering arm, and after it you read sampler tables the way the critics do, looking first for the classical baseline.

  4. 4

    foundation release

    DiffusionGemma Technical Report 2026two sittings

    Google DeepMind, the DiffusionGemma Team with 43 named authorstechnical report on arXiv, July 31, 2026too new to citecodedrawn in 1 figure

    Google fine-tuned Gemma 4 26B A4B into a uniform-noise diffusion model whose one set of weights runs causally over the history and bidirectionally over a 256-token canvas, using under 10% of the parent's training tokens. It writes 1,479 tokens a second for one user against 303 for the parent with MTP, trails by 19 points on AIME 2026, and loses on throughput past about 32 concurrent requests.

    Late-2026 arguments in this avenue get checked against this model, and two of the three projects run or rebuild it. Google released weights and no training code.

    skip Section 8, the downstream fine-tuning toolkit, and the multimodal material. Read Sections 2 to 4 for the noise and architecture, 5 for the stage that raised tokens per forward from 5 to nearly 20, and 6 for serving.
Reward tilting6 papers, about 24 hours
  1. 1

    result

    Probabilistic Inference in Language Models via Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo 2024two sittings

    University of Toronto and Vector Institute, Roger GrosseICML 2024, best paper awardat least 93 citationscode37drawn in 2 figures

    Casts red-teaming, sentiment control, and infilling as sampling an unnormalized target, learns twist functions that estimate each prefix's expected future potential with a contrastive loss tied to soft RL, and adds bidirectional SMC bounds on log Z that estimate KL in both directions.

    It treats the soft value as a thing you learn and then check, which most later entries assume, and its bounds are the one exactness check in this avenue that scales.

    skip The infilling experiments.
  2. 2

    foundation release

    Flow-GRPO: Training Flow Matching Models via Online RL 2025an afternoon

    CUHK MMLab and Kuaishou's Kling team, Wanli OuyangNeurIPS 2025at least 36 citationscode2,547drawn in 2 figures

    Turns the flow ODE into an SDE so that each denoising step is a Gaussian policy, adds GRPO with a per-step KL in closed form, and lifts SD3.5-M's GenEval from 63% to 95% and its text rendering from 59% to 92%. Its repository is what most GRPO work on flows forks.

    Section 4 and appendix B.3 hold the two facts behind most of what practice does to the tilt, the default noise level of 0.7, below the √2 at which the tuned model's ODE samples land on the tilt, and a per-step KL whose weight shrinks toward high noise.

  3. 3

    result

    Reinforce Adjoint Matching: Scaling RL Post-Training of Diffusion and Flow-Matching Models 2026two sittings

    Stefanie Jegelka, Nikolas Nüsken, and Carles Domingo-Enrich among the senior authorspreprinttoo new to citecode89drawn in 2 figures

    Notes that the KL-regularized optimum shifts only the clean-endpoint law, then regresses the velocity onto the pretraining target corrected by reward on the model's own samples, with no SDE rollouts, adjoint solves, or reward gradients. On SD3.5-M it reports GenEval 0.97 in 270 steps and OCR 0.97 in 60, against Flow-GRPO's 0.95 and 0.92.

    It decides whether exactness arrives with a cost win. Read Table 2 against the text, since the 50x comes from training curves, the table's step counts give at least 18x on GenEval, and the text concedes Flow-GRPO keeps more image quality on OCR.

  4. 4

    result

    Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model? 2025an evening

    Tsinghua LeapLab, Gao HuangNeurIPS 2025 oralat least 1,125 citationscode354

    Across model families and six RL algorithms, RLVR-trained models beat their bases on pass@k at small k and lose at large k.

    Under any correctness tilt pass@k can only rise at every k, so this large-k deficit is the cleanest evidence that RLVR samples no tilt of its base. It frames the weekend project and the argument heard at any lab doing reasoning RL.

  5. 5

    result

    Reasoning with Sampling: Your Base Model is Smarter Than You Think 2025an evening

    Harvard, Yilun DuICLR 2026 oralat least 90 citationscode457

    Samples p^alpha from a base model by Metropolis-Hastings over suffixes and reports MATH500 0.748 on Qwen2.5-Math-7B against GRPO's 0.785, at 8.84 times the tokens, with no training or verifier.

    Sections 4 and 5 give Algorithm 1 and a token arithmetic that leaves out the resampling overhead, which made one MATH500 run take about 30 GPU-hours with the reference code. The weekend project checks this paper.

  6. 6

    result

    GRPO-Guard: Mitigating Implicit Over-Optimization in Flow Matching via Regulated Clipping 2025an evening

    Jing Wang with Flow-GRPO's Jie Liu and Pengfei Wan, senior author Xiaodan LiangCVPR 2026at least 47 citationscode

    Finds that Flow-GRPO's importance ratios have a mean below 1 and a variance that differs by denoising step, which lets the proxy reward climb while gold quality falls, and fixes that by normalizing the ratios and reweighting gradients per step.

    It is the one paper that plots proxy against gold for GRPO on flows, and its per-step diagnosis is the nearest published work to the semester project's question.

Flow maps and one-step generation7 papers, about 30 hours
  1. 1

    result

    How to build a consistency model: Learning flow maps via self-distillation 2025two sittings

    Nicholas Boffi at CMU, with Michael Albergo and Eric Vanden-EijndenNeurIPS 2025no reliable countcode150drawn in 2 figures

    Derives a tangent condition that characterizes the flow map three equivalent ways, shows consistency models, consistency trajectory models, and shortcut models are special cases, and builds Lagrangian, Eulerian, and progressive self-distillation losses, with the Lagrangian one best on CIFAR-10 and the Eulerian one unstable.

    The debate between Eulerian and Lagrangian objectives running through this avenue becomes one argument, and it is the paper the semester project ports.

    skip The appendix proofs
  2. 2

    seminalAverage-velocity training from scratch, and the JVP-free surrogates, stability fixes, and ports to pixels, speech, and robot actions that followed

    Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling 2025an evening

    Kaiming He's group at MIT with Zico Kolter at CMU, Zhengyang Geng first authorNeurIPS 2025, oralat least 31 citationscode619drawn in 2 figures

    Trains a network on the average velocity over an interval through an identity tying it to the instantaneous velocity by a time derivative computed with a JVP, reporting one-step FID of 3.43 on ImageNet-256 and 2.92 on unconditional CIFAR-10.

    Seventeen months of MeanFlow variants read as edits to one equation, and you can say where the JVP enters.

    skip The ImageNet system comparison, which the avenue marks dead as a ranking
  3. 3

    result

    Simplifying, Stabilizing and Scaling Continuous-Time Consistency Models 2024two sittings

    OpenAI as of the paper, Cheng Lu and Yang SongICLR 2025, oralno reliable count

    Introduces TrigFlow, traces instability to the time-derivative term and fixes it with tangent normalization, adaptive weighting, and positional time embeddings, and writes a FlashAttention-style kernel computing attention and its JVP in one pass, scaling continuous-time consistency to 1.5B parameters and 1.88 FID at two steps on ImageNet-512.

    The avenue's sections on the JVP tax and the endpoint problem read as consequences of choices you have watched someone make.

    skip The discretization-error analysis if short on time
  4. 4

    result

    Can Push-forward Generative Models Fit Multimodal Distributions? 2022an afternoon

    Antoine Salmona with Valentin De Bortoli, Julie Delon, and Agnès DesolneuxNeurIPS 2022at least 3 citations

    Proves that a Lipschitz push-forward of a Gaussian stays a fixed total-variation and KL distance from a target with well-separated modes, with the gap set by the separation and the Lipschitz constant, and observes stacked stochastic models escaping the bound in experiments.

    One theorem explains why one-step students blur and why the large recipes add an adversarial or DMD term.

    skip Everything but the main theorem and the experiments
  5. 5

    foundation release

    Large Scale Diffusion Distillation via Score-Regularized Continuous-Time Consistency 2025two sittings

    NVIDIA with Jun Zhu's group at Tsinghua, Kaiwen Zheng first authorICLR 2026no reliable countcode

    Scales continuous-time consistency to Wan2.1 14B and Cosmos-Predict2 with a parallelism-compatible FlashAttention-2 JVP kernel, finds sCM alone loses fine detail to its mode-covering divergence, and adds score distillation as a mode-seeking regularizer, reaching VBench 84.92 at four steps against the teacher's 83.58.

    You learn what production flow-map distillation contains and costs, and rcm/utils/flash_attention_jvp_triton.py is the file to read before trusting a benchmark of JVPs through attention.

    skip The video evaluation details

    seminalThe drifting branch, its kernel and optimal-transport fields such as W-Flow and DriftXpress, encoder-free variants such as Teacher-Feature Drifting, and the long-short flow-map reading that ties it back to flow maps

    Generative Modeling via Drifting 2026an evening

    Kaiming He's group at MIT, Mingyang Deng first author, with Yilun DuPreprintno reliable countcode562drawn in 2 figures

    Trains a one-step generator against an anti-symmetric field, attraction to data minus repulsion from other generated samples, computed in a pretrained self-supervised feature space, reaching 1.54 FID in latent space and 1.61 in pixels, and the authors could not make it work on ImageNet without a feature encoder.

    You can state the strongest case that flow maps are unnecessary for one-step images and name the dependency it rests on.

    skip The system comparison, after Section 3, Table 3, and the robotics table

    Lan Feng first author with Alexandre Alahi senior, affiliations not checkedPreprinttoo new to cite

    Maps the design space of matching feature distributions under frozen encoders, finds MMD strong once estimated well and the generated batch the operative variable with an optimum above 2,048, shows any single encoder can be driven below the real-data score while images stay fake, and scores generators by a sliced-Wasserstein distance over 14 encoders, on which iRDM reaches 1.30.

    You can explain why this avenue marks one-step ImageNet FID dead, and you know which knob to protect in the Drifting port.

Discrete, edit, and diffusion language models3 papers, about 9 hours
  1. 1

    result

    Scaling Beyond Masked Diffusion Language Models 2026an evening

    Cornell Tech and NVIDIA, first author Subham Sekhar Sahoo, senior authors John Thickstun at Cornell and Ante Jukić at NVIDIAICML 2026, postercount not retrievedcode37

    The first scaling-law study of uniform-state and interpolating discrete diffusion. Masked models get about 12% more FLOPs-efficient from a plain cross-entropy loss, and at 1.7B uniform-state models have worse validation perplexity yet beat both masked and AR models on GSM8K.

    Argue the noise question from this paper, more than from the DiffusionGemma report, which made its choice without an ablation. After it, uniform noise stops being a story about self-correction and becomes a measured trade between likelihood and sampling, and 37 stars on the code behind the central 2026 noise result mean few people have rerun it.

  2. 2

    result

    The Flexibility Trap: Rethinking the Value of Arbitrary Order in Diffusion Language Models 2026an evening

    Tsinghua University, senior author Gao HuangICML 2026, Outstanding Paper Awardcount not retrievedcode

    On LLaDA-Instruct, confidence-ordered decoding matches AR order at Pass@1 and flattens as k grows, 67.1% against 83.0% Pass@128 on HumanEval, because the model postpones the high-entropy tokens where a solution forks. Scoring the model left to right and running plain GRPO reaches 89.1% on GSM8K and keeps parallel decoding.

    People cite it to say arbitrary order does not pay for reasoning. Its Pass@k analysis is the part this avenue turns on.

  3. 3

    result

    Diffusion Beats Autoregressive in Data-Constrained Settings 2025an evening

    Carnegie Mellon University, senior authors Deepak Pathak and Katerina FragkiadakiNeurIPS 2025, postercount not retrievedcode128

    Trains 200 models from 7M to 2.5B parameters on 25M to 100M unique C4 tokens and finds that masked diffusion keeps gaining from repeated data, with a fitted R_D* near 500 against about 31 for AR, and overtakes AR above a critical compute that grows as U to the power 2.174. At 100M unique tokens the best losses are 3.55 for diffusion and 3.71 for AR.

    The case for pretraining diffusion models natively rests on this paper, and its code is a Megatron fork, which is the gap the semester project fills.

    skip Read Section 3 and Appendix Figure 8, where attention dropout and token masking fail to help AR, since that appendix is what the semester project re-tests.

    Columbia, MIT and Toyota Research Institute, Cheng Chi first with Shuran Song and Russ Tedrake seniorRSS 2023, extended in IJRR 2024at least 649 citationscode4,626drawn in 2 figures

    Represents a visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising process over action sequences, run with a receding horizon, and reports a 46.9 percent average gain over prior methods on 12 tasks from four benchmarks. Later policy papers open by building on it.

    You know the diffusion half, so read it for action chunks, receding-horizon execution and visual conditioning, the vocabulary each later paper here assumes.

    Max Simchowitz's group at CMU, Chaoyi Pan first, with Guanya Shi and Nicholas Boffi among the authorsICLR 2026 poster, arXiv version 3 February 2026no reliable countcode

    Across 28 behavior-cloning benchmarks, finds that neither multimodality nor expressivity explains why generative policies win, credits supervised iterative computation with training noise, and shows a two-pass regression policy, MIP, matching flow, 82.2 against 81.6 on LIBERO-10 with pi0.

    The field disagrees with itself in public over this paper, and the nano's closing table tests the claim on one backbone.

    A 450M VLA, a frozen SmolVLM2 cut to half its text layers plus a 100M flow expert, that reaches 87.3 percent on LIBERO without robot pretraining and trains on one GPU.

    Physical Intelligence with UC Berkeley and Stanford, Karl Pertsch first and Sergey Levine seniorRSS 2025at least 751 citations

    Compresses action chunks with a discrete cosine transform before tokenizing, so autoregressive VLAs learn high-frequency dexterous skills where per-step binning fails, and pi0 with FAST matches the diffusion pi0 at up to 5x less training.     Physical Intelligence, 56 authors including Kevin Black, Chelsea Finn, Karol Hausman and Sergey Levinepreprintno reliable count

    RECAP trains a value model on returns, labels each action with a binarized advantage token, forces human corrections positive, and trains the flow VLA with its ordinary losses on the labeled data, more than doubling throughput and roughly halving failures on some of the hardest tasks.

    It is how Physical Intelligence improves its flow policies from experience, and the industrial counterpart to QAM, which you have read.

    CMU LeCAR Lab, Haoru Xue first, Guanya Shi seniorICRA 2025 by Semantic Scholar's venue field, while the arXiv page still says submittedat least 113 citationscode1,008

    Reads MPPI as a single diffusion step and anneals the sampling noise across iterations and along the horizon, cutting MPPI's tracking error 13.4 times on a quadruped by its abstract (its Table I gives 7.9 to 9.6 times) and beating RL policies by 50 percent on climbing, with no training.

    It is the control result that undercuts the generative-planning branch, and after it FlowMPC, LeWAM and D-MPC read as ways to add learning to a loop that already works without any. The weekend project ports it.

    comma.ai, Mitchell Goff first, with Harald Schäfer and George HotzCVPR 2025 Workshopsno reliable count

    Trains a rectified-flow DiT with future anchoring on driving video and a policy that imitates the world model's suggested actions near on-policy, ships the result in openpilot, and passes 24 of 24 MetaDrive lane-center tests where off-policy imitation passes 5.

    Its Table 2 gives the world-model policy the worst off-policy trajectory error of the three, 0.394 against 0.361, while its on-road engagement led the reprojective policy's, a fact worth carrying into any argument about offline evaluation. The semester project rebuilds it.

    seminalThe Boltzmann generator branch, a flow proposal reweighted with exact likelihoods, and with it the question of how importance weights behave as systems grow.

    Frank Noé's group, FU Berlin, with Simon Olsson, Jonas Köhler, and Hao WuScience 365, eaaw1147 (2019), published; arXiv 1812.01729at least 750 citationsdrawn in 2 figures

    Trains invertible flows to map a Gaussian onto a many-body Boltzmann distribution, by energy and by example, and reweights the samples with exact likelihoods, shown on condensed-matter systems and proteins.

    Scalable Boltzmann generators for equilibrium sampling of large-scale materials 2026an evening

    Jutta Rogal and Frank Noé, Maximilian Schebek firstNature Communications 17, 5010 (June 2026), published; preprint September 2025at least 1 citationscode14

    Flows whose conditioners see only each atom's neighbors are trained by energy on small cells and transferred to 1,728 molecules of mW ice, with joint ESS falling from 64.7 percent at 64 molecules to 0.02 percent at 1,728 while free energies per molecule stay within a thousandth of kT up to 1,000 molecules.

    The blocker in one table, and after it you can say why intensive quantities survive the collapse and extensive ones do not, which is what the three-week project measures.

    skip The silicon phase diagram.

    Mila and AITHYRA, Alexander Tong and Joey Bose with Yoshua Bengio, Danyal Rehman firstICML 2026, spotlighttoo new to citecode26

    The current record and the competing branch's best case, and after it you can judge the binning and SMC claims and run Robin yourself. No tempering arm appears in it, which is the weekend project's opening.

    Oxford, Cambridge, and coauthors elsewhere, Saifuddin Syed senior with Arnaud Doucet, Leo Zhang firstICLR 2026no reliable count

    Places normalizing flows, diffusion models, or controlled diffusions between tempering rungs as transports run in parallel, so parallel tempering keeps its asymptotic guarantees, and reports 10 to 100 times more round trips at small chain counts on a 40-mode mixture and 2.3 times on alanine dipeptide.

    NVIDIA GenAIR; Tomas Geffner and Kieran Didi, with Arash Vahdat and Karsten Kreis seniorICLR 2025, oralno reliable countcode278drawn in 2 figures

    Trains a non-equivariant transformer on roughly 21M AlphaFold DB structures with hierarchical fold-class conditioning, adds LoRA fine-tuning and classifier-free and auto-guidance for backbones, and generates designable proteins up to 800 residues. The field cites it as the scaling result and as the open stack to build on.

    It is the model two of the three projects run, and its README documents a different sampling noise scale per released checkpoint, which is the fact the weekend project is built around.

    skip The architecture ablations; read the metrics section and the sampling recipe
  2. 2

    result

    Rethinking Self-Consistency in Protein Generative Models 2026an afternoon

    Columbia; Minji Lee, with Mohammed AlQuraishi seniorICML 2026 workshop on generative and agentic AI for biology, poster, not main tracktoo new to citedrawn in 2 figures

    Self-consistency, the field's standard plausibility test, rejects 44 percent of native sequence and structure pairs. The failures split into flexibility failures and folder failures, both concentrated in flexible proteins, and ensemble self-consistency against conformational ensemble predictors restores native recall without losing specificity on a Rosetta decoy set.

    After this the metric every paper in the avenue reports stops reading as ground truth, which is the premise behind the weekend project and the follow-on to it.

  3. 3

    benchmark

    Is Retrieval All You Need? Assessment and Emergence of Novelty in Protein Structure Generation 2026an evening

    Tongyue Xu and Yijie Zhang, with Cheng Tanpreprinttoo new to cite

    Segments generated backbones into domains, searches them with Foldseek against 34,653 non-redundant CATH S40 domains, and reports how often a generated backbone contains a retrievable known domain. It then builds RetFold, a zero-training CPU baseline that assembles backbones out of retrieved domains and clears the same screens at two orders of magnitude lower cost.

    It is the paper the two-week project reimplements, and Table 1 plus the pLDDT split between retrieved fragments and inserted linkers are the numbers to hit. It also gives you the vocabulary to argue about novelty with numbers.

    skip The embedding-ensemble retrieval details, unless reimplementing stage one

    Scaling Atomistic Protein Binder Design with Generative Pretraining and Test-Time Compute 2026two sittings

    NVIDIA GenAIR with Mila, Oxford and Seoul National; Kieran Didi first, with Vahdat and Kreis seniorICLR 2026, oraltoo new to cite

    The Proteina-Complexa method paper, which calls generation versus hallucination a false dichotomy and pairs a pretrained generative prior with inference-time optimization under normalized compute budgets. Its abstract carries none of the experimental hit rates, which come from a separate September 2026 bioRxiv preprint, and names none of the specific search strategies, which appear on the project page instead.

    Reading it is how you can say, with a citation, that 2026's results came from search against a verifier rather than from a better transport objective, which is the single most useful position to hold in this avenue.

    Protein FID: Improved Evaluation of Protein Structure Generative Models 2025an afternoon

    MIT CSAIL; Felix Faltings and Hannes Stark, with Tommi Jaakkola and Regina Barzilaypreprint, v3 2025-07-23no reliable count

    Proposes a distributional metric for protein structure generators in a learned latent space, shows it behaves sensibly under perturbation and recovers Foldseek clusters and the CATH hierarchy, and concludes that current models do not match the PDB distribution.

    It sets the boundary of what a distributional metric certifies, which is what the retrieval project has to claim beyond. Read it before inventing any new score.

    Puts Riemannian flow matching on the crystal manifold, handling fractional coordinates on a torus, lattice parameters and atom types jointly, and reports roughly three times fewer integration steps than the diffusion baselines at comparable quality.

    benchmark

    InverseBench: Benchmarking Plug-and-Play Diffusion Priors for Inverse Problems in Physical Sciences 2025an evening

    Caltech with Johns Hopkins and NVIDIA, Yisong Yue last author, Katherine Bouman among the senior authorsICLR 2025, spotlightno reliable countcodedrawn in 2 figures

    Compares 14 plug-and-play diffusion methods with domain baselines on optical tomography, MRI, black-hole imaging, seismology, and fluid dynamics. Diffusion methods win from a cold start with a good prior, lose to supervised E2E-VarNet and to warm-started classical solvers, cost more compute, and move 0.48 dB against 9.58 dB for end-to-end methods when the MRI mask changes.

    After it you can place any guided-sampler paper in a table and name the one property, insensitivity to a changed forward operator, that a generative prior has over supervised inversion.

    University of Liège, Joeri Hermans first, Gilles Louppe seniorTMLR, November 2022at least 31 citationsdrawn in 2 figures

    Expected-coverage tests on neural posterior estimation, neural ratio estimation, sequential neural likelihood, and ABC variants with the correct simulator show that each can return overconfident posteriors, and ensembles of posterior surrogates are more conservative.

    UT Austin with UC Berkeley, authors listed alphabetically with Eric Price the senior onepreprint, revised 2025at least 2 citations

    If one-way functions exist, some posterior sampling problems with a diffusion prior force every algorithm into superpolynomial time even though unconditional sampling is fast, and rejection sampling is close to optimal under a stronger assumption.

    This is where the field disagrees with itself, and after it you can say why the guided-posterior node needs a calibration benchmark more than another sampler.

What to build

Three per avenue, written as a curriculum. Each teaches something the other two do not, so do all three in order.

Reward tiltingDo them in order. The weekend power sampler makes the tilt concrete with no reward model and no training, twisted SMC then adds an external reward, learns the soft value the exact methods estimate, and bounds how far a sampler sits from its target, and the semester project moves to fine-tuning, where the question is whether hitting the target is worth it when the reward is a proxy. Together they cover inference-time tilting, soft value estimation, and choosing the tilt at the decoding, sampling, and training layers.

Flow maps and one-step generationThe weekend measures the trade this avenue is about, sharp images against coverage, on released FLUX.1-dev students without training anything. The Drifting port then builds the rival that skips the ODE by borrowing a feature space, and the semester file builds the flow map itself and prices its derivative. Do them in that order, because the weekend tells the two training projects what to measure beyond FID and the Drifting port is the shorter build with the public payoff. The weekend reliably works, the port may land high for silent reasons, and the semester's ending experiment may not separate the camps.

Discrete, edit, and diffusion language modelsDo the weekend vLLM sweep first, since about ten GPU-hours show on real hardware why a diffusion model's speed is a one-user advantage. The nano comes next and builds the kind of model the weekend served from an AR checkpoint, testing DiffusionGemma's uniform noise at 1.5B. The semester project comes last because it needs the cluster, and it tests data efficiency, the one argument under which pretraining a diffusion model from scratch would repay its cost.

Flow and diffusion models in controlThe three cover planning with a known model, the action expert with its two imitation rivals, and the world model as a simulator, which are the avenue's branches outside the critic-as-energy direction. Do them in order: DIAL-MPC on Playground's Go1 teaches sampling-based MPC and sets the bar a generative planner must clear, the nanoVLA builds the action expert the companies ship and tests whether its flow matters, and the comma rebuild trains the simulator itself and asks how faithful it must be before a policy trained inside it drives. The first two should work and the third may not, which is deliberate.

Learned sampling from unnormalized densitiesDo them in order. The weekend builds the OpenMM and replica-exchange setup and the habit of counting energy calls and GPU-seconds on the avenue's record holder, the three weeks put you inside a Boltzmann generator you wrote so the extensive-KL wall becomes your own curve, and the semester carries the replica-exchange arm to transition paths, where short MD supplies exactness.

Molecules, proteins, and materialsThe three cover evaluation, data provenance, and a generator written from scratch, which is the ground an outsider with one GPU and no laboratory can take in this avenue. Do them in order: project 1 builds the sampling and scoring setup and teaches what designability is made of, project 2 reuses that scorer to ask how much of a generated structure is retrieved rather than invented, and project 3 leaves proteins for crystals, where you write the transport model yourself and the benchmark's dependence on an unpinned potential is the finding. Project 1 reliably works, project 3 may not reach the number, and that difference is deliberate.

Transport between datasets and scientific inferenceThe three cover the avenue's three working checks: a second event generator in particle physics, lineage barcodes in single-cell biology, and the exact likelihood in gravitational-wave inference. Do them in that order, since the weekend teaches a collaboration's validation habits on six observables, the two-week project scores a learned coupling against measurements the method never saw, and the semester builds the one setup here where the check is part of the method. Projects 1 and 3 should work, and project 2 may end in a table where nothing beats PRESCIENT's 2021 number, which would be a result.

Media generation and servingStart with the weekend, which installs the Wan 2.1 stack and a timing harness that the two-week project reuses on LongLive. The two-week project moves from what a clip costs to why a stream degrades after its teacher's horizon, and the semester leaves video for speech, the branch whose design has settled and where latency is what buyers pay for. All three run on one GPU.

A weekend

Reward tilting

Power sampling on stock vLLM, checked against likelihood best-of-N

nano, end to end

Write the power sampler from Karan and Du's ICLR 2026 paper for Qwen2.5-Math-7B as one short vLLM script, reproduce its MATH500 score, and check whether keeping the most likely of about nine ordinary samples does as well on the same token budget.

Power sampling and likelihood best-of-N, matched token for token

Power sampling and best-of-N ranked by the base model’s own likelihood both push toward the model’s likely answers, so the fair test spends the same decoded tokens on each, about nine samples’ worth at the paper’s settings.

Switch the pivotal tokens. With one, a single early token decides the answer, and the best of 12 likelihood-ranked samples beats 10 steps per block at the same tokens on this toy, 0.97 to 0.69. With two or three, one per block, the block-by-block chain wins, 0.56 to 0.42 and 0.33 to 0.12, because best-of-N needs one sample with every pivot right. The chain stays short of p⁴ after 10 steps. The right panel is the paper’s Table 1, with the project’s ±0.02 band around 0.748 and the row the project adds.

Flow maps and one-step generation

What four FLUX.1-dev students keep of their teacher

apply something that exists

Generate the same 100 prompts with FLUX.1-dev and four of its fast students, pi-FLUX, SenseFlow, Hyper-FLUX, and FLUX Turbo Alpha, measure how much of the teacher's range of images each student still produces, and test whether letting FLUX.1-dev take the first step brings the lost range back.

Coverage sees what spread and preference miss

A student can spread as wide as its teacher, or look as good, and still miss part of the teacher’s range, which only coverage of the teacher’s own samples shows, and one teacher step brings back only the layouts a student has down-weighted.

The blurred student spreads wider than the teacher, 3.39 against 3.16, and covers 0.81 of the teacher’s samples against the teacher’s own 0.92. The student missing a layout matches the teacher’s spread and density and still covers only 0.81. One teacher step lifts the sharpened student from 0.84 to 0.88 and leaves the other two where they were, since the blurred student’s first step already matches the teacher’s and the missing layout never comes back. The project calibrates first, reproducing pi-FLUX’s OneIG diversity of 0.229 within 0.01.

The self-swap test catches a sigma shifted twice

A student that hands over to itself must reproduce its own samples exactly, and passing already-shifted sigmas back to diffusers shifts them again, so every remaining step runs at a noise level the state does not have.

At 1,024 pixels, 4,096 image tokens and a shift of 3.16, the state after the first step sits at sigma 0.957 and the model is told 0.986. Its samples move 0.58 from the native ones, and the share off the five layouts rises from 14% to 61%. Passed on as they are, the sigmas reproduce the native samples exactly. At 256 tokens the shift is 1.65 and the samples still move 0.12, so the test fails at every size.

Discrete, edit, and diffusion language models

DiffusionGemma against Gemma 4 under load, in vLLM

apply something that exists

Serve Google's DiffusionGemma and the ordinary Gemma 4 it was made from on one H100 with vLLM, raise the number of simultaneous users from 1 to 64, and find where the ordinary model starts winning on total speed.

Where Gemma 4 with MTP overtakes DiffusionGemma, in a model of one H100

A diffusion step computes a 256-token canvas for every request, so once the GPU is busy the tokens kept per pass decide the race, and a model built only from the report’s one-user numbers puts the crossover near Google’s measured 32.

At the report’s 19.74 tokens per pass, with sampling that grows with each request as in Google’s untuned runs, the model’s crossover is 28 requests. Batched sampling pushes it past 64, and 10 tokens per pass pulls it to 11. On memory, one fp32 buffer per slot fits 65 slots at utilization 0.85, three fit 33, and four fit 27, below the crossover. Two constants are fitted to the report’s one-user steps, and the rest comes from the model config, the report, and NVIDIA’s H100 datasheet.

Flow and diffusion models in control

DIAL-MPC against PPO on MuJoCo Playground's Go1

apply something that exists

Port DIAL-MPC, a planner that tries thousands of simulated futures every 20 ms and trains nothing, onto MuJoCo Playground's Go1 walking task and measure it against the PPO policy Playground trains in minutes.

DIAL against MPPI at equal samples and at equal rollouts

DIAL repeats MPPI's weighted average several times per control step with shrinking noise, which beats MPPI at equal samples per pass, and the project's table asks how much of that lead survives equal compute.

Pick the samples per pass and press Play. At 8 samples MPPI's error is 0.79 m/s against DIAL's 0.24, a 3.3× gap. Given the 32 rollouts DIAL spends there, MPPI falls to 0.43, a 1.8× gap, and at 128 samples the gap is 1.1×. A fixed LQR policy, standing where PPO's line goes, tracks at 0.13 and beats every planner on these smooth dynamics. DIAL's abstract reports 13.4× against MPPI, while its own Table I gives 7.9× and 9.6×.

Learned sampling from unnormalized densities

Robin against replica exchange on 30 unseen octapeptides

apply something that exists

Run Robin, the model that holds the record for sampling unseen peptides, and plain replica exchange in OpenMM on the same 30 octapeptides, and count the energy calls and GPU-minutes each needs to reach the same accuracy.

Energy error against energy calls: a learned sampler, MD and replica exchange

A sampler trained on related systems pays a few thousand energy calls per new molecule, so the project's number is the budget at which replica exchange reaches the same energy error, and how many molecules repay the training.

Every arm starts in the minor basin. At full transfer error the learned sampler's 2,000 proposals reach an E-W2 of 0.12 at an ESS near 1%. MD is still near 1 at 10⁶ calls. Replica exchange, eight replicas from 310 to 450 K, matches the learned sampler near 800,000 calls, about 400 times its budget. Raise the model cost to count GPU time, the project's second axis. Robin reports 3.615 at 2×10⁵ energy evaluations, the number the project's run must land within 10% of.

Molecules, proteins, and materials

The designability curve, swept across models

apply something that exists

Protein backbone papers report designability at one or a few noise settings, so run Proteina and FrameFlow across eight noise scales with one scorer and plot the curve those numbers sit on.

Designability against diversity as the noise scale moves

Lowering the noise scale in Proteina's sampler pulls samples into the dense cores of the data, so designability rises while diversity falls, and every published designability number is one point on that curve.

Move the noise scale from 1 toward 0.1. On this toy designability climbs from 25% to 83% while diversity falls from 0.96 to 0.23, and the deterministic sampler lands near the target's own 29%. Proteina's tables already trace part of its curve: M_FS gives 98.2% at γ = 0.35, 96.4% at 0.45 and 91.4% at 0.50, and 19.6% from its ODE. The shaded box is the done-when, 96.4% within three points.

Transport between datasets and scientific inference

SBUnfold and OmniFold in one PyTorch file

reimplement a paper

Rebuild SBUnfold and OmniFold in one PyTorch file on the public Pythia and Herwig Z+jets jets, match the paper's six-observable table, then swap the Pythia tune and see how far the unfolded answer moves.

Only iterating sheds the simulation's prior

SBUnfold's deterministic bridge lands closer to the truth than OmniFold's first step on a one-dimensional toy with an exact detector, but both answers move with the simulation's prior, and only OmniFold's iterations pull the three priors' answers together.

Start at one iteration with prior C. For all three priors the bridge lands closer to the truth than OmniFold's first step, as SBUnfold found on four of six observables. Raise the iterations and OmniFold passes the bridge at the third, and its dashed spread across the priors drops below the bridge's, which has no iterations to shrink it. Widen the detector smearing and every answer leans further toward its prior. Three toy mixtures stand in for Pythia tunes 21, 25, and 26, and on this toy an ideal conditional generator, such as a perfect cINN, gives exactly OmniFold's first step.

The table a reproduction has to land in

SBUnfold's Table II gives each method's EMD on six observables, and the reproduction is done when both its OmniFold step and its bridge land inside the 30 percent band around the printed numbers on at least five of them.

With 600,000 Herwig events SBUnfold has the lower EMD on four observables, and OmniFold's first step wins on jet mass and constituent multiplicity; bold rows are SBUnfold's. Switch to 1,000 events and SBUnfold leads on all six, since OmniFold is the only method that trains on the data events. A reproduction passes when its own numbers fall in the shaded bands on at least five rows for both methods, and the better method matches the table on at least five.

Media generation and serving

TurboDiffusion, timed end to end on one RTX 4090

apply something that exists

TurboDiffusion says it makes a five-second Wan 2.1 clip in 1.9 seconds, a figure that leaves out the text encoder and the video decoder, so time text encoding, denoising, and decoding on one RTX 4090, then swap in three published fast decoders and measure what each saves in seconds and loses on VBench.

The reported 1.9 seconds leave out the longest stage

Flash-VAED's timings put the stock Wan decoder at 3.3 to 4.2 seconds per five-second clip on a 5090-class card, 1.7 to 2.2 times TurboDiffusion's whole denoiser, so a clip takes about three times the reported 1.9 seconds before text encoding is counted.

Every bar is a model built from published numbers: TurboDiffusion's 1.9 seconds on an RTX 5090, scaled by 4/3 for four steps with top-k's cost left out, and decoder times from Flash-VAED's runs on an RTX 5090 D. At half a second of text encoding, row A takes 6.6 seconds, decoding is 64 percent of it, and Flash-VAED brings row B to 3.7 seconds, faster than the five seconds of video it makes. Switch the decoder to Self Forcing's run, which decodes a stream in chunks, and Wan's decode drops to 3.3 seconds, still the longest stage. Drag text encoding up, as when the 11.36 GB umT5 encoder has to run on the CPU of a 24 GB card, and the headline's share shrinks further. The project replaces every bar with RTX 4090 measurements whose stages sum to within 5 percent of the wall clock.

Reward tilting

Twisted SMC in PyTorch, reproducing the ICML 2024 KL table

reimplement a paper

Rewrite the ICML 2024 best paper on twisted sequential Monte Carlo in PyTorch and reproduce its table of how closely each method samples the TinyStories-33M stories a toxicity classifier flags, which that model almost never writes.

Table 2, measured where the answer is known

Table 2’s two columns are one proposal’s KL divergence from the target in each direction, both read through a single estimate of log Z, so an error in log Z moves them by the same amount in opposite directions.

At twist strength 0.35 the toy’s exact divergences, 1.38 and 1.13 nats, sit near the paper’s contrastive row, and with 500 particles every seed lands within 0.10 of them. Lose the exact sample and cut the particles to 8: log Z comes out 0.33 low, so KL(q‖σ) reads 1.04 and KL(σ‖q) 1.43, both outside the band on opposite sides. At strength 1 the twist is exact and both read 0.

Flow maps and one-step generation

Drifting in PyTorch on GPUs, matched to its 8.46 ablation

reimplement a paper

Port Drifting, Kaiming He's group's one-step image generator, from JAX documented for TPUs to PyTorch on eight GPUs, and match the paper's 8.46 ImageNet FID for its small ablation model.

Which slips the 8.46 check can see

Slips that keep the drifting field at zero when generated samples already match the data cost the paper at most about 2 FID points, slips that break that balance cost 33 to 169, and on a toy, dropping the self-mask breaks it.

The port as written leaves a net drift of 0.01 or less at every distance. Softmax over y only, no kernel normalization, a single temperature, and per-rank batch means stay within 0.02 of zero, and the paper scored the ones it ablated between 8.67 and 10.62, three of them inside or on the edge of the band, where the check cannot tell them from the port as written. 1.5× attraction pulls samples in by 0.44 of a step and scored 41.05, and attraction only pulls by 0.78 and scored 177.14. Dropping the self-mask pulls by 0.32, and no published row warns a port about it.

Discrete, edit, and diffusion language models

Fast-dLLM v2's conversion in one file, with uniform noise as a switch

nano, end to end

Turn Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct into a diffusion model twice in one short script, once with masking and once with the random-token noise Google used for DiffusionGemma, and compare both with NVIDIA's released Fast-dLLM v2 on GSM8K.

One block decoded with masks and with uniform noise

A mask tells the model which positions are unknown, and uniform noise makes it work that out from the tokens themselves, which costs passes when random tokens can pass for real ones and buys the chance to revise a kept token.

With masks, every threshold from 1.0 down to 0.5 decodes a coherent block, at up to 4 tokens per pass, and at 0.4 the arm keeps all eight marginal guesses at once and spells a block no template has. With uniform noise at b = 0.1 and random tokens that fit one time in 64, the block stays coherent at 1.11 tokens per pass, with 0.31 revisions per block. When random tokens fit one time in 8 it falls to 0.50 tokens per pass, and at one in 256 it rises to 1.54. Which arm a trained 1.5B model favors on GSM8K is the project’s measurement, with the masked row within 3 points of the released checkpoint’s 62.0.

The training forward the conversion reproduces

Fast-dLLM v2 trains on a noisy copy and a clean copy of each sequence side by side, so a noisy block sees itself and the clean blocks before it, and each token is predicted one position earlier, the habit the AR checkpoint already has.

Rows are queries and columns keys. The noisy copy’s second block sees itself and the clean first block, never its own clean tokens, and the clean copy runs block by block. Under masks only the masked positions carry a label, and the complementary view labels the rest, so each token is trained once per pair of views. Switch to uniform noise and every position of the noisy copy carries a label, since a corrupted token looks like any other, the change the project’s convert.py makes.

Flow and diffusion models in control

nanoVLA: SmolVLA in one file, then four action heads

nano, end to end

Write SmolVLA as one PyTorch file that trains on LIBERO to within three points of its published 87.3%, then swap its flow-matching head for two-step regression, plain regression, and FAST tokens on the same backbone and see which hold up.

Four action heads, each at its optimum on one toy

On demonstrations that split above and below an obstacle, regression averages the two routes, the two-step head snaps to the majority route, and the flow and token heads sample both, at 1, 2, 10 and 8 network passes.

At an even split, regression and the two-step head both return the average route, through the obstacle. From 51% the two-step head's second pass lands on the majority route, while regression clears only from 67%. Flow and tokens sample both routes at every split. Each panel is its loss's exact optimum on this toy, and Much Ado About Noising finds multimodality is not the main reason generative policies work, so the project's table may find a tie.

What the four-head table can tell apart

A suite score is an average of pass or fail episodes, so binomial noise alone decides how large a gap between two heads the table orders reliably at 10 or 50 trials per task.

With every task at 80%, SmolVLA's 10 trials per task give one LIBERO-10 score 4.0 points of binomial error, and 50 trials with two seeds give 1.3. SmolVLA's 5-point gap between flow and L1 regression is a four-suite average, which 10 trials order right 96% of the time. MIP's 0.6-point lead over flow on LIBERO-10 comes out right 63% of the time even at 50 trials with two seeds. Seed variance adds to all of these.
